rows.rule: The caller passes an identity, never a secret; the broker injects server-side. Generated app code and model context never hold a third-party token.
rows.evidence: most consistent finding across the commercial survey; no OSS runs this direction

rows.rule: Tenant key on every connection from the first migration, per-tenant key derivation, stable externalId

Every action declares naturally-idempotent / idempotent-with-key / unsafe; the runtime refuses to auto-retry unsafe. Same key with a different payload is a hard error via request fingerprint. Replay returns the saved status and body with an explicit replay receipt header.
rows.evidence: most-starred idempotency-key middleware found is 14 stars; hono-idempotency is a specification to reimplement, not a dependency

rows.rule: Stripe is the positive control and the shape to copy

contract.supply: client-generated key in the Idempotency-Key header, up to 255 chars, UUIDv4 or derived from a user-attached object such as a cart ID
contract.lifetime: pruned after at least 24 hours; a key reused after pruning generates a NEW request, so replay protection silently lapses rather than erroring
contract.replay_identical: status code and body of the first request are saved regardless of success or failure and returned on retry, including cached 500s, with an Idempotent-Replayed: true header as the machine-readable receipt
contract.replay_different_params: the layer compares incoming parameters against the original and errors when they differ
contract.methods: all POST; GET and DELETE are idempotent by definition and keys have no effect
contract.concurrency: HTTP 409 Conflict when two requests share a key
contract.save_boundary: results are saved only after endpoint execution begins, so validation failures and concurrent conflicts save nothing and may be retried
contract.retry_signal: Stripe-Should-Retry: true|false tells the client whether retrying is worthwhile; absent means undetermined
contract.five_hundreds: treat as INDETERMINATE - the cached response will not change but Stripe may reconcile and fire webhooks for objects created during reconciliation, so a cached 500 is not proof nothing happened; mitigation is sending a local identifier in metadata for cross-referencing

rows.critical_caveat: RATE LIMITERS RUN BEFORE THE IDEMPOTENCY LAYER. A request rate-limited with a 429 can produce a different result with the same idempotency key. The same applies to a 401 with a missing key and most 400s with invalid params. An idempotency key therefore does NOT make a request universally safe to replay - the safety window begins only once the request reaches the API's idempotency layer.
rows.actionist_consequence: Actionist's own idempotency layer must sit INSIDE its rate limiter and auth check, not outside, or it inherits exactly this hazard at the host boundary

rows.rule: Honour Retry-After and observed 429 rates per connector rather than a fixed exponential curve; retry only what idempotency class permits
rows.note: commercial norm is retry WITHOUT idempotency, i.e. the industry default is the unsafe one

rows.rule: Per-tenant-per-connector fair share so one tenant cannot exhaust a shared third-party quota
rows.evidence: good per-process libraries, nothing shaped as per-tenant-per-connector quota

rows.rule: Consent graded by consequence not resource (read / reversible / irreversible-or-financial), defaulting to the middle tier, expressible as a composable workflow step
rows.evidence: OpenAI's three-tier consent; Workato is the only surface where approval is a workflow step rather than a platform modal

rows.rule: First-class action mode returning the exact resolved outbound request with no side effect, on by default, not tenant-disableable
rows.evidence: Zapier preview_only, the best primitive found; Zapier AI Actions itself is discontinued so study, do not depend

rows.rule: One queryable per-tenant ledger of every attempt, retry, replay, denial and approval; receipts deliberately exclude payload bodies
Allow-list derived from the connector manifest, bound to a proxy that can refuse the call
rows.evidence: OPA and Cerbos decide, neither enforces; no surveyed project ships the pairing for tool calls

rows.rule: When a tenant has multiple accounts for one provider the action must name which
rows.evidence: Pipedream silently selects the most-recently-created account, a documented ambient-authority defect class

rows.rule: Browser connectors are a separate authority class from API connectors
rows.evidence: Browserbase Contexts replay cookies and tokens with MFA completed once and reused, a durable bearer blob outside any scope or revocation model, plus ToS exposure from stealth and IP-rotation features

invariants.statement: Catalogue, credential runtime, connection store and action runtime are four separate governed components
The caller passes an identity, never a secret
Every connection is keyed by tenant from the first migration with per-tenant key derivation and a stable externalId
Every action declares its idempotency class and the runtime refuses to auto-retry the unsafe class
Replay with the same key and a different payload is a hard error, enforced by request fingerprint
invariants.source: Stripe docs read 2026-08-27: sending the same idempotency key with different parameters produces an error indicating the new request did not match the original
invariants.correction: An earlier draft of this invariant asserted 'non-2xx is not cached'. Stripe's actual documented behaviour is the OPPOSITE: it saves the status and body of the first request regardless of whether it succeeds or fails, and returns cached 500s. The claim originated in the hono-idempotency README's summary of the Stripe rule and did not survive reading Stripe's own docs. Actionist must decide this deliberately rather than inherit it: caching failures gives a stable replay answer but can pin a transient error, while not caching them permits a genuine retry to succeed.

invariants.statement: The idempotency layer sits inside the rate limiter and the auth check, never outside
invariants.source: Stripe documents that rate limiters run BEFORE its idempotency layer, so a 429 can produce a different result under the same key

invariants.statement: Consent is graded by consequence, not by resource
Dry-run is a first-class action mode and is not tenant-disableable
One per-tenant action ledger; receipts exclude payload
No ambient authority in account selection
Egress is allow-listed from the connector manifest and bound to an enforcing proxy
